claims.statement: Leonardo's own memoranda and draft report on the defense of the Isonzo line in Friuli, proposing a movable weir to control the river's level against Ottoman incursion (Itinerario tier A)

background.text: The material witness of the stay is the profile portrait of Isabella d'Este in the Louvre, black and red chalk, its outlines pricked for transfer. The pricking implies a workshop procedure of replication, consistent with Gusnasco's report that copies were being seen. For years afterward Isabella pressed Leonardo, through intermediaries, to convert the drawing into a painted portrait; he never did. The correspondence generated by that unconsummated negotiation is itself the principal source, documenting at once the working of Mantuan cultural diplomacy and the logic by which Leonardo selected and declined commissions.

Leonardo arrived in the immediate aftermath of Zonchio, when Ottoman cavalry had raided as far as Friuli. What the Republic wanted from a foreign engineer was not painting but river engineering, and the Isonzo memoranda show it: a movable barrier to flood the valley at will and deny the passage. The conception is of the same grammar as the Arno diversion he would propose to Florence in 1503, and confirms that Leonardo's hydraulics formed a consistent defensive science across employers. The stay was brief; no painting commission is recorded.
